classification: Researcher-selected finite experimental configuration, not owner budget or WAN/annual service guarantee
architecture_question: Can a 96-distinct ordinary-payment block complete bounded producer/archive/destination transport, genuine validation, atomic durable commit and accounted retention?

transport.topology: producer -> archive -> receiving validator, distinct processes on one Linux host
transport.latency_policy: once per request/response; not once per data chunk
transport.pacing_policy: cumulative actual application bytes including protocol framing/retries; report overhead not covered by this application-byte model
transport.kernel_page_cache: uncontrolled/warm unless an actual cold condition is established; no cache-dropping privilege assumption

queue_limits.validator_decoded_api_copies: measure actual RSS; frame cap does not mean only one in-memory copy

archive.retention: durable full bytes; ACK after file and directory persistence, not proof-validity attestation

validator.retention: explicit local RETAIN; charge full body/database/journal growth, no pending mandatory export or eviction

storage.scope: finite experiment headroom only; not annual participant cost allocation

control_boundaries: coherent mutated final real proof reaches proof rejection, full state unchanged, valid followup
interrupted bounded transfer accepts no partial block
durable commit/publication before lost ACK, restart and current-canonical exact retry without double application

measurement.correctness_oracle: outside measured role processes and spans
measurement.receiving_source_access: actual producer DB and fixture paths inaccessible; only bounded socket data enters
required: proof verification counts and preparation/cache conditions
measurement.stage_gate: review actual Gate1 before generating larger distinct workload; a failure triggers repair/pivot, never automatic scale-up
